rounds.text: Mizzen Ventures Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of 2.32x compared to a sector benchmark of 4.93x [E7], indicating that investors are paying significantly less for the company's asset base than they would for its peers. Furthermore, the company's P/E ratio stands at 115.98x, which sits below the sector benchmark of 126.99x [E6], offering a relative discount on earnings compared to the broader market. This relative undervaluation is reinforced by the enterprise value to EBITDA multiple of 61.19x, which trades at a substantial discount to the sector benchmark of 102.59x [E11]. Conceded: the absolute price-to-book is 2.89x [E2], the P/E reaches 206x according to filed statements [E1], a discounted cash flow calculates intrinsic value at ₹ 13 per share [E34], and the stock sits at the very bottom of its 52-week range [E5].

Conceded: the company's EV/EBITDA of 61.19x sits below the sector benchmark of 102.59x [E11], and its P/E of 115.98x trails the sector's 126.99x [E6]. However, pointing to these relative sector discounts masks the extreme absolute multiples found in the filed statements, where the P/E reaches an alarming 206x [E1] and the price-to-book sits at 2.89x [E2]. Furthermore, relying on sector benchmarks ignores the company's inferior operational efficiency, demonstrated by an ROA of just 1.87% against a sector benchmark of 3.94% [E8]. The bull's highlighted P/B discount relative to peers [E7] offers little comfort when the stock is pinned at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range, occupying 0% of its range [E5]. Finally, these relative comparisons completely collapse under rigorous cash flow analysis, which reveals an intrinsic value of only ₹ 13 per share against a market price of ₹ 65.4 [E34], generating a devastating margin of safety of -396.6% [E35].

blind_spot_facts.fact: A reverse DCF says today's price already implies 41.2% earnings growth, against the 18.0% the base case assumes.
Bias check — Valuation blind-spot: Rich valuation — P/E 206, P/B 2.9, DCF overvalued 397%. Even with a decent story, a lot of optimism is already in the price.
